# 0. Introduction and data preparation

This report explores county-level prison admission rates, and how they changed from 
2006 to 2014. The 'county-prison-admissions.csv' dataset contains admission counts, admission rates,
and associated county populations. 'CountyClassifications.csv' contains the economic type of the counties,
and the population loss status of the counties. 'People.csv' contains the population estimates for the counties, specifically 
in TotalPopEst2014, which was renamed Population2014.

FIPS identifiers are used to merge the datasets. The use of left joins ensures that all counties in the prison dataset are retained, even if they do not have corresponding entries in the other datasets. The final combined dataset includes county-level prison admission data, classifications, and population estimates for analysis.
Missing values are preserved 
```{r, include = FALSE}
# Data importing - County Prison Admissions
CountyPrisonAdmin <- read.csv('/Users/lloydtodaro/Desktop/STA141/county-prison-admissions.csv')

dim(CountyPrisonAdmin)
names(CountyPrisonAdmin)
str(CountyPrisonAdmin)
head(CountyPrisonAdmin)
colSums(is.na(CountyPrisonAdmin))
summary(CountyPrisonAdmin)
```

```{r, include = FALSE}
# Data importing - County Classifications
CountyClass <- read.csv('/Users/lloydtodaro/Desktop/STA141/CountyClassifications.csv')

dim(CountyClass)
names(CountyClass)
str(CountyClass)
head(CountyClass)
colSums(is.na(CountyClass))
summary(CountyClass)
```

```{r, include = FALSE}
# Data importing - People
People <- read.csv('/Users/lloydtodaro/Desktop/STA141/People.csv')

dim(People)
names(People)
str(People)
head(People)
colSums(is.na(People))
summary(People)
```

```{r, include = FALSE}
prison <- CountyPrisonAdmin
classifications <- CountyClass
people <- People

names(classifications)[1] <- "FIPS"
names(prison)[names(prison) == "fips"] <- "FIPS"

prison$FIPS <- sprintf("%05d", as.integer(prison$FIPS))
classifications$FIPS <- sprintf("%05d", as.integer(classifications$FIPS))
people$FIPS <- sprintf("%05d", as.integer(people$FIPS))

people <- people |>
  filter(FIPS %in% prison$FIPS)

```

```{r, include = FALSE}
prison$admissions2014 <- as.numeric(
  gsub(",","", prison$admissions2014)
)
# removed commas, now checking for NAs
class(prison$admissions2014)
sum(is.na(prison$admissions2014))
```

```{r, include = FALSE}

class_selected <- classifications |>
  filter(Attribute %in% c(
    "RuralUrbanContinuumCode2013",
    "Metro2013",
    "Type_2015_Update",
    "Population_loss_2015_update"
  )) |>
  select(FIPS, Attribute, Value)

class_wide <- class_selected |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = Attribute, values_from = Value) |>
  mutate(
    rural_urban = factor(
      RuralUrbanContinuumCode2013,
      levels = 1:9,
      labels = c(
        "Metro: 1 million or more",
        "Metro: 250,000-999,999",
        "Metro: under 250,000",
        "Nonmetro: 20,000+, adjacent",
        "Nonmetro: 20,000+, not adjacent",
        "Nonmetro: 2,500-19,999, adjacent",
        "Nonmetro: 2,500-19,999, not adjacent",
        "Nonmetro: under 2,500, adjacent",
        "Nonmetro: under 2,500, not adjacent"
      )
    ),
    metro_status = factor(
      Metro2013,
      levels = c(0, 1),
      labels = c("Nonmetro", "Metro")
    ),
    economic_type = factor(
      Type_2015_Update,
      levels = 0:5,
      labels = c(
        "Nonspecialized",
        "Farm-dependent",
        "Mining-dependent",
        "Manufacturing-dependent",
        "Federal/State government-dependent",
        "Recreation"
      )
    ),
    population_loss = factor(
      Population_loss_2015_update,
      levels = c(0, 1),
      labels = c("Other county", "Population-loss county")
    )
  )

people_2014 <- people |>
  filter(Attribute == "TotalPopEst2014") |>
  select(FIPS, Population2014 = Value)

anyDuplicated(class_wide$FIPS)
anyDuplicated(people_2014$FIPS)
```

```{r, include = FALSE}
combined <- prison |>
  left_join(class_wide, by = "FIPS") |>
  left_join(people_2014, by = "FIPS")

table(classification_match = prison$FIPS %in% class_wide$FIPS)
table(people_match = prison$FIPS %in% people_2014$FIPS)

prison |>
  anti_join(class_wide, by = "FIPS") |>
  select(FIPS, county, state)

prison |>
  anti_join(people_2014, by = "FIPS") |>
  select(FIPS, county, state)
```

```{r, include = FALSE}
with(combined, table(valid06, is.na(admitsPer10k2006), useNA = "ifany"))
with(combined, table(valid13, is.na(admitsPer10k2013), useNA = "ifany"))
with(combined, table(valid14, is.na(admitsPer10k2014), useNA = "ifany"))
```

```{r, include = FALSE}
combined |>
  select(
    starts_with("admissions"),
    starts_with("admitsPer10k"),
    starts_with("population20"),
    Population2014
  ) |>
  summary()

combined |>
  filter(!is.na(admitsPer10k2014)) |>
  arrange(desc(admitsPer10k2014)) |>
  select(
    FIPS, county, state, admitsPer10k2014,
    admissions2014, population2014, source
  ) |>
  head(10)
```

# 1. What does prison admission look like for a typical U.S. county?

```{r, results = 'hide'}
rate2014 <- combined |>
  filter(!is.na(admitsPer10k2014), valid14 == "TRUE")

rate2014 |>
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    mean = mean(admitsPer10k2014),
    median = median(admitsPer10k2014),
    sd = sd(admitsPer10k2014),
    Q1 = quantile(admitsPer10k2014, 0.25),
    Q3 = quantile(admitsPer10k2014, 0.75),
    IQR = IQR(admitsPer10k2014),
    min = min(admitsPer10k2014),
    max = max(admitsPer10k2014)
  )
```



```{r, fig.width = 4, fig.height = 3.5, out.width = '48%', fig.show = 'hold'}

ggplot(rate2014, aes(x = admitsPer10k2014)) +
  geom_histogram(
    aes(y = after_stat(density)),
    binwidth = 5, boundary = 0,
    fill = "steelblue", color = "white"
  ) +
  geom_density(color = "blue") + 
  labs(
    title = "Bin width: 5",
    x = "Admissions per 10,000 residents (2014)",
    y = "Density"
  )

ggplot(rate2014, aes(x = admitsPer10k2014)) + 
  geom_histogram(
    aes(y = after_stat(density)),
    binwidth = 10, boundary = 0,
    fill = "steelblue", color = "white"
  ) +
  geom_density(color = "blue") +
  labs(
    title = "Bin width: 10",
    x = "Admissions per 10,000 residents (2014)",
    y = "Density"
  )
```

(explain histogram)


# 2. Which counties appear to have the largest prison-admission problem?

```{r, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 3.5}
count_data <- rate2014 |>
  filter(!is.na(admissions2014)) |>
  mutate(county_state = paste(county, state, sep = ", "))

top_counts <- count_data |>
  slice_max(admissions2014, n = 10)

top_rates <- count_data |>
  slice_max(admitsPer10k2014, n = 10)

ggplot(top_counts, aes(
  x = admissions2014,
  y = reorder(county_state, admissions2014)
)) +
  geom_col(fill = "red") + 
  labs(
    title = "Counties with the most prison admissions in 2014",
    x = "Number of admissions",
    y = NULL
  )

ggplot(top_rates, aes(
  x = admitsPer10k2014,
  y = reorder(county_state, admitsPer10k2014)
)) +
  geom_col(fill = "red") + 
  labs(
    title = "Counties with the highest prison-admission rates in 2014",
    x = "Admissions per 10,000 residents",
    y = NULL
  )
```

# 3. How did county prison-admission rates change from 2006 to 2014?

```{r, results = 'hide'}
change_data <- combined |>
  filter(
    !is.na(admitsPer10k2006),
    !is.na(admitsPer10k2014),
    valid06 == "TRUE",
    valid14 == "TRUE"
  ) |>
  mutate(change = admitsPer10k2014 - admitsPer10k2006)

change_data |>
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    increases = sum(change > 0),
    decreases = sum(change < 0),
    unchanged = sum(change == 0),
    median = median(change),
    Q1 = quantile(change, 0.25),
    Q3 = quantile(change, 0.75),
    within_10 = sum(abs(change) <= 10)
  )

change_data |>
  slice_max(change, n = 3) |>
  select(county, state, change)

change_data |>
  slice_min(change, n = 3) |>
  select(county, state, change)
```

```{r, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 3.5}
ggplot(change_data, aes(x = change)) +
  geom_histogram(
    binwidth = 5, boundary = 0,
    fill = "red", color = "white"
  ) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(
    title = "Changes in prison-admission rates (2006-2014)",
    x = "Change in admissions per 10,000 residents",
    y = "Number of counties"
  )
```

```{r, fig.width = 4, fig.height = 4, out.width = '60%'}
ggplot(change_data, aes(
  x = admitsPer10k2006,
  y = admitsPer10k2014
)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, color = "red") +
  coord_equal() +
  labs(
    title = "County prison-admission rates",
    x = "2006 admissions per 10,000 residents",
    y = "2014 admissions per 10,000 residents"
  )
```

# 11. Which counties deserve individual attention?

```{r}
cutoff <- quantile(rate2014$admitsPer10k2014, 0.75) +
  1.5 * IQR(rate2014$admitsPer10k2014)

unusual <- rate2014 |>
  filter(admitsPer10k2014 > cutoff)

selected <- unusual |>
  slice_max(admitsPer10k2014, n = 5)

selected |>
  transmute(
    County = paste(county, state, sep = ", "),
    Rate = admitsPer10k2014,
    Admissions = admissions2014,
    Population = population2014
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "latex",
    booktabs = TRUE,
    digits = 2,
    row.names = FALSE,
    col.names = c("County", "Rate", "Admissions", "Population"),
    align = "lrrr"
  )
```

```{r, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 5}
ggplot(population_data, aes(
  x = people_population2014,
  y = admitsPer10k2014
)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_point(
    data = selected,
    color = "blue", size = 3
  ) +
  geom_text(
    data = selected,
    aes(label = county),
    hjust = 0, angle = 25, size = 3
  ) +
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = cutoff,
    linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  scale_y_continuous(
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0.05, 0.2))
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Counties with exceptionally high admission rates",
    x = "2014 population estimate (log10 scale)",
    y = "Admissions per 10,000 residents"
  )
```

# 12. Is Dearborn County unusual even when compared with counties like itself?

```{r}
dearborn <- rate2014 |>
  filter(FIPS == "18029")

others <- rate2014 |>
  filter(FIPS != dearborn$FIPS)

comparisons <- bind_rows(
  "All U.S. counties" = others,
  
  "Indiana" = others |>
    filter(state == "IN"),
  
  "Similar population" = others |>
    filter(
      people_population2014 >= 0.75 * dearborn$people_population2014,
      people_population2014 <= 1.25 * dearborn$people_population2014,
    ),
  
  "Same rural-urban category" = others |>
    filter(rural_urban == dearborn$rural_urban),
  
  "Same economic type" = others |>
    filter(economic_type == dearborn$economic_type),
  
  "Same rural-urban and economic type" = others |>
    filter(
      rural_urban == dearborn$rural_urban,
      economic_type == dearborn$economic_type
    ),
  
  .id = "reference_group"
)

comparisons |>
  group_by(reference_group) |>
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    median = median(admitsPer10k2014),
    maximum = max(admitsPer10k2014)
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "latex",
    booktabs = TRUE,
    digits = 2,
    row.names = FALSE,
    col.names = c("Reference group", "Counties", "Median", "Maximum"),
    align = "lrrr"
  )
```

```{r, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 4.5}
ggplot(comparisons, aes(
  x = reference_group,
  y = admitsPer10k2014
)) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "red") +
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = dearborn$admitsPer10k2014,
    color = "blue", linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
    scale_x_discrete(
    labels = function(x) stringr::str_wrap(x, width = 28)
  ) +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    title = "Dearborn compared with alternative reference groups",
    subtitle = "Blue dashed line: Dearborn's 2014 rate",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Admissions per 10,000 residents"
  )
```
# 13. What does the prison-admission story look like in our own county - Yolo County, California?

```{r, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 3.5, results = 'hide'}
yolo <- combined |>
  filter(FIPS == "06113")

yolo_time <- data.frame(
  year = c(2006, 2013, 2014),
  admissions = c(
    yolo$admissions2006,
    yolo$admissions2013,
    yolo$admissions2014
  ),
  rate = c(
    yolo$admitsPer10k2006,
    yolo$admitsPer10k2013,
    yolo$admitsPer10k2014
  )
)

yolo_time


ggplot(yolo_time, aes(x = year, y = rate)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(color = "blue", size = 3) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(2006, 2013, 2014)) +
  labs(
    title = "Yolo County prison admission rates",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Admissions per 10,000 residents"
  )
```

```{r}
yolo_others <- rate2014 |>
  filter(FIPS != yolo$FIPS)

yolo_groups <- bind_rows(
  "All U.S. counties" = yolo_others,
  
  "California" = yolo_others |>
    filter(state == "CA"),
  
  "Similar population" = yolo_others |>
    filter(
      people_population2014 >= 0.75 * yolo$people_population2014,
      people_population2014 <= 1.25 * yolo$people_population2014
    ),
  
  "Same rural-urban category" = yolo_others |>
    filter(rural_urban == yolo$rural_urban),
  
  "Same economic type" = yolo_others |>
    filter(economic_type == yolo$economic_type),
  
  "California population and rural-urban peers" = yolo_others |>
    filter(
      state == "CA",
      rural_urban == yolo$rural_urban,
      people_population2014 >= 0.5 * yolo$people_population2014,
      people_population2014 <= 2 * yolo$people_population2014
    ),
  
  .id = "reference_group"
)

yolo_groups |>
  group_by(reference_group) |>
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    median = median(admitsPer10k2014)
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "latex",
    booktabs = TRUE,
    digits = 2,
    row.names = FALSE,
    col.names = c("Reference group", "Counties", "Median"),
    align = "lrr"
  )
```

```{r, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 4.5}
ggplot(yolo_groups, aes(
  x = reference_group,
  y = admitsPer10k2014
)) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "red") +
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = yolo$admitsPer10k2014,
    color = "blue", linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
    scale_x_discrete(
    labels = function(x) stringr::str_wrap(x, width = 28)
  ) +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    title = "Yolo County in context",
    subtitle = "Blue dashed line: Yolo's 2014 rate",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Admissions per 10,000 residents"
  )
```

```{r, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 2.5}
metro_summary <- metro_data |>
  group_by(metro_status) |>
  summarise(
    median = median(admitsPer10k2014),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

ggplot(metro_summary, aes(
  x = median,
  y = metro_status
)) +
  geom_point(size = 3, color = "steelblue") +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = sprintf("%.2f", median)),
    vjust = -0.8
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 25)) +
  labs(
    title = "Median 2014 admission rates",
    x = "Median admissions per 10,000 residents",
    y = NULL
  )
  ```
